To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

overexpressed minibrain kinase/DYRK1A is a novel component of NFTs and granules in granular vacuolar degeneration in patients with Down syndrome and sporadic Alzheimer’s Disease, and that the overexpression is associated with an increase of DYRK1.
the overexpression of DYRK-1A protein is associated with an increase of DYRK- 1A positive neurofibrillary pathology in a gene dosage dependent manner.
DYRK1a is overexpressed in DS and that it is associated with NFT formation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the gene DYRK1A located in the Down Syndrome critical region on chromosome 21 in neurofibrillar degeneration.
the role of DYRK1 protein in the early development of neurofibrillar degeneration in DS.
the role of overexpresssed DYRK1A kinase in the early onset and the severity of neurofibrilary degeneration in patients with DS.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
DYRK1As role in the early onset and progression of neurofibrilary degeneration in patients with Down syndrome is a complex issue and the results presented in this study are not conclusive.
overexpression of DYRKIA contributes to neurof fibrillary degeneration in patients with DS more significantly than it contributes to neurofbrillary degeneration in sporadic AD.
DYRK1a is not a cause of AD but is a factor in the pathogenesis of AD in DS.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
DYRK1a is a key kinase in the development of neurofibrillar degeneration in AD and DS.
DYRK1a plays a role in neurofibrilary degeneration in Down Syndrome and Alzheimer's Disease, but the exact role is not yet known.
overexpression of DYRK-1A is involved not only in NFD, but also in granulovascular degeneration and corpora amylaceus.
The main takeaway from our work is that
overexpression of DYRKIA contributes to the early onset and severity of neurofibrillar degeneration in patients with DS.
the DYRK1a kinase is involved in the neurofibrillary pathology that is a hallmark of Alzheimer disease and Down syndrome.
overexpressed minibrain kinase/DYRK1A contributes in the early onset neurofibrillary pathology in DS.
